ShortDef: A regularly updated list of the ten most critical web application security risks.
Details: Covers broken access control, cryptographic failures, injection, insecure design, misconfiguration, vulnerable components and more. A common baseline for reviews and training.
WhenToUse: A starting checklist for any web application review.

ShortDef: Untrusted input is treated as code (SQL, shell, template) and executed.
Details: The fix is to keep data and commands apart: parameterised queries, safe APIs instead of shell strings, and strict validation. Escaping by hand is fragile.
WhenToUse: Anywhere user input reaches a database, a shell, an LDAP query or a template.

ShortDef: An attacker's script runs in another user's browser because the site printed untrusted input unescaped.
Details: Stored, reflected and DOM-based variants. Defend with output encoding, framework auto-escaping, a Content Security Policy and HttpOnly cookies.
WhenToUse: Any page that shows user-provided content.

ShortDef: A malicious page makes your browser send a request to a site you are logged in to.
Details: Because browsers attach cookies automatically, the site cannot tell the request was not intended. Use anti-forgery tokens and SameSite cookies.
WhenToUse: Any state-changing request authenticated by cookies.

ShortDef: Browser rules about which other websites may call your API from JavaScript.
Details: A misconfigured policy (reflecting any origin with credentials) lets hostile sites read your users' data. CORS is not authentication.

ShortDef: Users can do or see things their role should not allow, such as changing an ID in a URL to read someone else's data.
Details: The top item in the OWASP list. Check permissions on the server for every request and every object; never rely on hiding buttons.
WhenToUse: Every endpoint that returns or changes data.

ShortDef: Proving who you are: passwords, one-time codes, security keys and passkeys.
Details: Store passwords only as salted slow hashes (Argon2, bcrypt, PBKDF2). Add multi-factor authentication; passkeys resist phishing. Lock out and rate-limit repeated failures.

ShortDef: Storing a deliberately slow, salted fingerprint of a password instead of the password.
Details: Fast hashes like MD5 or SHA-256 let attackers try billions of guesses per second. Argon2id, bcrypt and PBKDF2 are slow on purpose, and a unique salt defeats precomputed tables.

ShortDef: How a site remembers you after login: session cookies or tokens.
Details: Cookies should be HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite. Rotate on login, expire sensibly, and make logout and 'sign out everywhere' actually invalidate sessions. JWTs need short lifetimes and a revocation plan.

ShortDef: Scrambling data so only holders of a key can read it, in transit (TLS) and at rest.
Details: Use well-reviewed libraries and modern defaults; never invent your own algorithm. Protect keys more carefully than the data, and rotate them.
WhenToUse: Any sensitive data crossing a network or sitting on disk.

ShortDef: Keeping passwords, tokens and keys out of code and delivering them safely at runtime.
Details: Never commit secrets; scan history for leaks and rotate anything exposed. Use a vault or the platform's secret store, inject via environment, and give each secret the least access.
WhenToUse: Every application with credentials to other systems.

ShortDef: Give every person, service and token only the access it needs, no more.
Details: Limits what a stolen credential or a bug can do. Applies to database users, cloud roles, API scopes and file permissions.
WhenToUse: Designing roles, service accounts and tokens.

ShortDef: Checking that data has the expected type, length and format before using it.
Details: Validate on the server, allow-list what is acceptable, and still encode output for its context. Validation reduces risk but does not replace parameterised queries or escaping.
WhenToUse: At every trust boundary: forms, APIs, files, headers.

ShortDef: Known security holes in the libraries you use, tracked as CVEs.
Details: Most code in an app is someone else's. Keep a software bill of materials, scan with tools such as Dependabot or Trivy, and patch quickly, prioritising what is actually reachable.
WhenToUse: A routine part of every release.

ShortDef: Compromising software through something it depends on: a package, a build tool or an update channel.
Details: Examples: malicious look-alike packages, hijacked maintainer accounts, poisoned CI. Pin and verify dependencies, use lockfiles, review new packages and limit CI permissions.
WhenToUse: Assessing how you consume third-party code.

ShortDef: Thinking through what could go wrong with a design before building it.
Details: Draw the data flows, mark trust boundaries, and ask what an attacker could spoof, tamper with, leak or break (STRIDE). Cheap to do early, expensive to fix late.
WhenToUse: Designing any feature that handles sensitive data or new entry points.

ShortDef: Capping how often a client can try something, to slow abuse and guessing.
Details: Apply to login, password reset, search and expensive endpoints, by IP and by account. Combine with lockouts and alerting.
WhenToUse: Any public endpoint an attacker could hammer.
